chief_complaint: thick itchy pink scar expanding beyond border of ear piercing
hpi_details: A 47-year-old man has a slowly enlarging, itchy pink scar extending beyond the border of a prior ear piercing, consistent with a keloid.
ideas: He thinks his old ear piercing hole became chronically infected or had an allergic reaction to metal that caused abnormal scar tissue to build up.
concerns: He is worried that the bump will continue to expand across his ear and draw stares and remarks from colleagues.
expectations: He hopes the doctor can freeze or cleanly snip off the bump today so his earlobe looks normal again.

clinical_knowledge.topic: Keloid Scar revision evaluation and management
core_concepts: Prompt recognition and structured assessment of Keloid Scar revision is essential for guiding targeted diagnostic workup and clinical decision-making.
A thorough clinical history, baseline risk assessment, and targeted objective testing must be synthesized rather than relying on any single symptom in isolation.
Standard management emphasizes Plan for Keloid Scar revision: Intralesional Triamcinolone injections, pressure earrings, laser, adapted to individual patient risk factors and clinical severity.
Diagnostic workup and therapeutic decisions should adhere to established clinical guidelines while accounting for patient-specific comorbidities.

history.answer: A raised, pink scar on my left earlobe where I had a piercing has been getting thicker and itchier, and it seems to be growing past the original hole.
I had my left ear pierced about twelve months ago, and this firm bump started growing about six months ago.
I got my left earlobe pierced at a tattoo and piercing shop a year ago; it was slightly red back then, but no other injuries there.
It started as a tiny hard bead around the hole, but it has steadily expanded over the last several months to about the size of a bean.
Yes, it has grown well beyond the edges of the original puncture hole into the surrounding earlobe skin.
Yes, it itches quite a bit, especially when I get hot or sweaty.
It does not ache on its own, but it feels slightly tender if I press hard on it or sleep directly on that side.
It feels very firm and rubbery when I touch it, not soft or filled with liquid.
It is a shiny, smooth pink color throughout, without any dark brown spots or black specks.
No, it has never bled spontaneously, cracked open, or formed crusty scabs.
No, there is no spreading redness around it, no heat, and no pus or foul odor draining out.
No, there is no central dark pore, and nothing like white cheese or paste comes out if pressed.
No, it does not get bigger or smaller from day to day; it has only grown larger over time.
No, I have checked my other ear and the rest of my body, and there are no other lumps like this anywhere.
I rubbed an over-the-counter scar gel on it for about three weeks, but it did nothing, and I have not had any injections or procedures done.
I work indoors, so my sun exposure is minimal, and I have never had a severe blistering sunburn.
No fever, no chills, no unintended weight loss, and no fatigue or drenching night sweats.
I thought the old piercing site just got irritated or reacted poorly to cheap metal and built up scar tissue.
I'm really self-conscious that it's going to keep expanding and that people at work won't stop staring at my ear.
I was hoping you could just freeze it off or cut it away in the clinic today so my ear looks normal again.
I do not have any chronic medical conditions like diabetes, high blood pressure, or immune problems.
I have never had any surgeries, hospitalizations, or other skin procedures in the past.
I do not take any prescription medications, immunosuppressant drugs, or herbal supplements.
I have no known allergies to medications, metals, or adhesives.
I have never smoked cigarettes or used tobacco products.
I only drink socially, maybe a glass of beer once or twice a month at social dinners.
I work as an office accountant and live with my wife and teenage son.
My mother tends to develop thick, raised scars after cuts or minor surgery, but no one in my family has ever had skin cancer.

exam.finding: Blood pressure 120/78 mmHg, heart rate 72 beats/min, respiratory rate 14 breaths/min, body temperature 36.6°C, oxygen saturation 99% on room air.
Alert, well-nourished, comfortable male in no acute distress.

A raised, firm, smooth pinkish-red nodule measuring approximately 1.5 cm by 1.0 cm on the left earlobe, extending clearly beyond the margin of the prior piercing site, without ulceration, crusting, or purulent drainage; external auditory canals and tympanic membranes are clear bilaterally.

The left earlobe nodule is rubbery-hard, freely mobile over deeper tissue without fixation, and mildly uncomfortable upon firm compression; full skin survey shows no other abnormal scars, cystic lesions, or dysplastic pigmented lesions.
No preauricular, postauricular, submandibular, or cervical lymphadenopathy palpable bilaterally.
